# Enflame GCU FlagGems Integration Test Results

Measured on an eight-device Enflame S60 host. Installation and configuration are
covered in [flaggems-setup.md](flaggems-setup.md).

The `flagos` device reuses the `u = 2` cut of the eight GCU dies, so
`torch.flagos.device_count()` reports 8 while the vendor runtime addresses 2
devices. Every measurement below was taken on `flagos:0`.

## Environment Setup

### Python Environment

- **Environment**: venv (`gcu-flagtree`), Python 3.12
- **Location**: `/public-flash/lvyufeng/venvs/gcu-flagtree`

### Package Versions

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| torch | 2.10.0+cpu |
| torch_fl | 0.1.0 (in-place `build_ext` against the working tree) |
| flagtree | 0.6.1+enflame3.6 |
| triton | 3.6.0 (bundled by flagtree, backends `{'enflame'}`) |
| flag_gems | `0.0+g3c6f7537d`, `vendor_name == 'enflame'` |

FlagGems is an editable install of master revision
`3c6f7537d2d5d3aa680c55bbee5c70f2100c5b85`. No `triton` *distribution* is
registered: flagtree installs its own `triton` package and the NVIDIA wheel has
to be uninstalled first (see [flaggems-setup.md](flaggems-setup.md)).

numpy is absent from this venv, and deliberately so. It is not a dependency of
the CPU torch wheel, and nothing on the GCU route imports it. pip warns at
install time that `flag_gems` declares a `numpy` requirement it cannot satisfy;
that warning is expected, because `flag_gems` is installed with `--no-deps` and
the GCU route never reaches a numpy import.

#### Host toolchain caveat (measurement box only)

The measurement box runs Ubuntu 22.04 / glibc 2.35. The flagtree wheel is built
for glibc >= 2.38 and takes exactly one symbol newer than that: the C23
`__isoc23_strtol`. On this box `import triton` therefore fails with

```text
ImportError: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
(required by .../site-packages/triton/_C/libtriton.so)
```

To take the measurements below, that one dynamic-symbol reference in the
*measurement venv's* `libtriton.so` was retargeted in place to glibc's existing
`strtol` (identical behaviour here; the C23 variant only adds `0b` prefix
parsing). The edit is width-preserving and touches no code, only the dynsym
name and the version-need entry, and it is **not** committed anywhere.

**CI needs none of this**: `.github/configs/gcu.yml` pins the
`flagtree-enflame3.6-py312-torch2.10.0-ubuntu24.04` image, whose glibc 2.39
satisfies the wheel as shipped. This has not been run through CI yet — the
change is still a local branch — so the claim rests only on that glibc version
comparison.

### Installation Steps

```bash
python3.12 -m venv /public-flash/lvyufeng/venvs/gcu-flagtree
source /public-flash/lvyufeng/venvs/gcu-flagtree/bin/activate
pip install torch==2.10.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu

python3 -m pip uninstall -y triton          # repeat until "not installed"
RES="--index-url=https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-hosted/simple"
python3 -m pip install "flagtree===0.6.1+enflame3.6" $RES
python3 -m pip uninstall -y torch_gcu triton_gcu

cd /tmp && git clone https://github.com/FlagOpen/FlagGems.git && cd FlagGems
git checkout 3c6f7537d2d5d3aa680c55bbee5c70f2100c5b85
pip install --no-deps -e .
pip install packaging 'PyYAML==6.0.1' 'sqlalchemy==2.0.48'
```

### Environment Variables

The shell used for every run below:

```bash
export TOPS_HOME=/opt/tops FLAGOS_ACCELERATOR=gcu GCU_KERNEL=1 FLAGGEMS_PYTHON=1 FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS=0
export PYTHONPATH=/public-flash/lvyufeng/PyTorch-Plugin-FL
source /public-flash/lvyufeng/venvs/gcu-flagtree/bin/activate
```

Rebuild the in-place extension after any change under `csrc/` or `scripts/`, and
re-run both generators after a change to the gap set:

```bash
python3 scripts/codegen/codegen_gcu_flaggems.py
python3 scripts/codegen/gen_vendor_confs.py
python3 setup.py build_ext --inplace
```

## Routing Configuration

`torch_fl/configs/backends_gcu.conf` is generated by
`scripts/codegen/gen_vendor_confs.py` and is FlagGems-first by construction: for every
one of the 2037 routable overloads the generator picks the first available
backend in the order `flaggems_cpp > flaggems > tileops > gcu > none`, then
re-routes everything in `NATIVE_TRITON_GAPS["gcu"]` to the native `topsaten`
kernel (`gcu`), or to `none` where topsaten has no kernel either and the call
reaches ATen's `cpu_fallback`.

| Route | Overloads | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `flaggems` | 255 | 12.5% |
| `gcu` (native topsaten) | 176 | 8.6% |
| `none` (cpu_fallback) | 1606 | 78.8% |
| **accelerated** | **431** | **21.2%** |

`backends_gcu.conf`, sha256
`366d986f0c7aa292eb398e9de8b3dd9a1533240fc4f026472299a3560245e40d` for the
change this file records, and
`4e8265afbf12b472097588ea1f7ae67f627b37711f2e3c17200f190588e0ea40` as committed
at the tip of this branch; the difference is the banner the `flagos/main` merge
rewrote, described below, plus the one route line and the coverage banner
upstream's `2f6b10c` adds to the op list this branch was rebased onto.

The banner line is the only part of either generated file that the merge with
`flagos/main` changed: the generator paths inside them moved from `scripts/` to
`scripts/codegen/` in `1f62f74`, so the hashes recorded before that merge
(`10b8ab4b…` for the conf, `39cd03e3…` for the `.inc`) differ from these without
any route or registration changing.

The previous revision routed 152 overloads to `gcu` and 1884 to `none`, with no
FlagGems route at all, so this is **152 -> 431 accelerated routes**. "Previous"
means the conf *committed* at the branch point -- `251c9c8`, and unchanged in
`flagos/main` at `bc39a83` -- which is what the wheel ships and what CI reads.
The two most recent revisions that touched that file (this one and `d0e2d1a`)
both ship zero `flaggems` routes. The generator is a different story and worth
separating out: it was already FlagGems-first for GCU at the branch point and
still is at `bc39a83`, emitting 88 `flaggems` routes, but no
`gcu_flaggems_register.inc` existed to back them, and the committed conf was
never regenerated -- `scripts/codegen/gen_vendor_confs.py --check` reports
`backends_gcu.conf` stale at both revisions. Regenerating alone would therefore
have shipped 88 routes pointing at an empty dispatcher slot. What this change
adds is the registration and the measured gap set that make the FlagGems-first
generation safe to ship.

The two counts reconcile with the generated registration:

- `csrc/aten/backends/gcu/generated/gcu_flaggems_register.inc` holds 248
  `m.impl` lines (`FLAGGEMS_PYTHON_OPS` minus the 227-op gap set, minus the
  ops `gcu_register.inc` already registers).
- 7 further `flaggems` routes are claimed natively first by
  `csrc/aten/backends/gcu/generated/gcu_register.inc` (`clamp`, `fmod.Tensor`,
  `gelu`, `mean`, `mean.dim`, `remainder.Tensor`, `silu`), which is where the
  255 comes from. `codegen_gcu_flaggems.py` computes its op list as
  `(FLAGGEMS_PYTHON_OPS - gaps) - native - pending` and omits those ops on
  purpose -- a second `m.impl()` for the same op and dispatch key would only
  override the first and warn at import -- so the conf still names `flaggems`
  as their route while the native kernel serves them. The routing table and the
  two registration files reconcile at `255 = 248 + 7`.
- `gcu_register.inc` registers 183 native ops; 7 of them are the ops just
  listed, and the other 176 are the `gcu` routes.

Every accelerated route is present in the registration its name implies: no op
is routed to `gcu` without a `gcu_register.inc` entry, so no route reaches a
registered-but-empty dispatcher slot.

A second, later change to the same conf moved eleven overloads from `none` to
`gcu` -- `arange`, `arange.start`, `arange.start_step`, `fill_.Scalar`,
`fill_.Tensor`, `masked_fill_.Scalar`, `masked_fill_.Tensor`, `zero_`,
`view_as_real`, `view_as_complex`, `linalg_vector_norm` -- which is the whole of
the +11 in the `gcu` column above and the whole of the -11 in `none`. It was
selected by census rather than by survey: a 50-step Qwen-Image-2512 run at
1024x1024 with `FLAGOS_LOG=fallback` recorded **80,536 `cpu_fallback` calls in
exactly six operators** (`fill_` 23,570, `zero_` 19,221, `view_as_complex`
18,794, `view_as_real` 18,794, `arange` 79, `linalg_vector_norm` 78) against
468,227 device dispatches, with no seventh operator anywhere in the log.
`view_as_real` and `view_as_complex` are the two handwritten metadata kernels in
`csrc/aten/strided_ops.cc`; everything else was generated. Within this conf
`gcu_register.inc` moves 152 -> 163 `m.impl` lines and
`gcu_flaggems_register.inc` keeps its 248 (only its banner's count of FlagGems
ops already claimed natively moves, 88 -> 97), so at that point the
reconciliations read `255 = 248 + 7` and `156 = 163 - 7`. No `flaggems` route was
touched.

A third change to the same conf moved three more overloads from `none` to `gcu`
-- `add.out`, `sub.out` and `mul.out` -- which is the whole of the remaining
`156 -> 159` in the `gcu` column and the `1625 -> 1622` in `none`. They were
selected the same way, by census rather than by survey: two Adam steps over a
five-parameter model with `FLAGOS_LOG=fallback` recorded **45 `cpu_fallback`
calls, 25 of them `aten::add` and 10 `aten::mul`**, all from the optimizer's own
state updates. Those two names were misleading -- `csrc/aten/fallback.cc:21`
logs `op.schema().name()`, so `add_.Tensor`, `add.out` and `add.Tensor` all
print as `aten::add` -- and ATen registers no PrivateUse1 kernel for
`add_.Tensor` / `sub_.Tensor` / `mul_.Tensor` at all: they are structured
in-place ops whose composite redispatches onto `add.out` / `sub.out` / `mul.out`
with `out=self`. The conf's `add_.Tensor = none`, `add_.Scalar = none` and the
`mul_.*` / `sub_.*` lines are therefore inert, and one kernel per `out=` spelling
serves both forms. `add.out` and `sub.out` are generated from the
`binary_alpha_out` template and `mul.out` from `binary_out`, all three through
`topsaten`, and the kernel sizes its output because the `out=` contract lets a
caller pass a zero-size or differently-shaped `out`. A cast guard
(`c10::canCast`) and an output device guard were added to these and to the three
pre-existing `out=` kernels `bmm.out`, `mm.out` and `addmm.out`. Two defects on
that path were fixed with it: `at::native::flagos::resize_` used to delegate to
the **CPU** `at::native::resize_`, whose `resize_bytes_cpu` copies the old bytes
with a host `memcpy` and therefore faulted on an HBM source, so growing an `out`
storage segfaulted; and `_copy_from` took its byte count from the source while
writing into the destination's dtype in both directions. Within this conf
`gcu_register.inc` moves 163 -> 166 `m.impl` lines
(`c6526ed3…` -> `f961aff0…`) and `gcu_flaggems_register.inc` keeps its 248 again,
so the reconciliations above are what the tree now reads: `255 = 248 + 7` and
`159 = 166 - 7`. Two of the moves this conf makes come off `flaggems` rather than
`none`: `_softmax` and `linalg_vector_norm` gained entries in the generator's
`NATIVE_TRITON_GAPS["gcu"]` set, so the route generated for both changed from
`flaggems` to `gcu`. That is the `257 -> 255` in the table, and
`linalg_vector_norm` leaving this file's own `m.impl` list is the `249 -> 248`.

A fourth change to the same conf moved twelve more overloads from `none` to
`gcu` -- `_upsample_nearest_exact2d[.out]`, `embedding_dense_backward[.out]`,
`index_select[.out]`, `index_fill.int_Scalar[_out]`, `index_fill.int_Tensor[_out]`,
`index_fill_.int_Scalar` and `index_fill_.int_Tensor` -- which is the whole of the
`159 -> 171` in the `gcu` column and the `1622 -> 1610` in `none`. Two censuses
picked them. A training step (two Adam steps over a five-parameter model with an
embedding lookup and an `index_select` path) with `FLAGOS_LOG=fallback` recorded
**11 `cpu_fallback` calls in four operators** -- `aten::index_select` 4,
`aten::embedding_dense_backward` 4, `aten::index_fill_` 2, `aten::nonzero_static`
1. The first three names cover all eight `index_*` / `embedding_dense_backward`
spellings above: `csrc/aten/fallback.cc:21` logs `op.schema().name()`, and an
in-place `index_fill_` reports as `aten::index_fill_` whichever value form it
took. A Qwen-Image-2512 VAE decode at 1024x1024 supplied the fourth name: it made
three `_upsample_nearest_exact2d` calls, all of them `cpu_fallback` on the
pre-change tree. After the change the same training step records **exactly one
`cpu_fallback` call**, `aten::nonzero_static`, with both step losses unchanged
(`-32.7952`, `-51.3676`), and the VAE decode reports `cpu_fallback ops: 0` and
runs to completion.

`aten::nonzero_static` is deliberately left on the fallback and is the only
remaining one on either path. Its result is `int64`, which
`TopsatenSupportsDtype` declines everywhere, so no `gcu` kernel can be written
for it; `flag_gems` ships no `nonzero_static` module, so there is no `flaggems`
kernel either; and the schema has no `out=` overload, so the FL layer's `out=`
lane cannot serve it. There is nothing to route it to, and the conf says `none`
because that is true rather than because the op was overlooked.

The kernels were added to the generator rather than by hand --
`scripts/codegen/codegen_gcu.py` gains the twelve overloads, twelve templates and
five helpers in `csrc/aten/backends/gcu/topsaten_common.h` -- and running it a
second time leaves all three generated artifacts byte-identical. Within this conf
`gcu_register.inc` moves 166 -> 178 `m.impl` lines
(`f961aff0…` -> `806d7ce7…`) and `gcu_kernels.cc` `35c8a37e…` -> `7f34288a…`,
while `gcu_flaggems_register.inc` keeps its 248 (`9c9c99d0…`), so the
reconciliations above are what the tree now reads: `255 = 248 + 7` and
`171 = 178 - 7`. The fourth change moves nothing off `flaggems`; all twelve of
its routes come from `none`.

Because registration and routing are checked against each other, the twelve ops
cannot be measured against the pre-change conf: with the new `gcu_register.inc`
in place and `none` still in the conf, the first `_upsample_nearest_exact2d` call
raises `routed to 'none' (no accelerated impl on this platform) but the op is
registered on PrivateUse1` instead of reaching `cpu_fallback`. The before-numbers
above therefore come from a build that predates the registration, and the after
numbers from a build that has both halves of the change.

A fifth change to the same conf moved five more overloads from `none` to `gcu` --
`all`, `index.Tensor`, `nonzero`, `nonzero_static` and `where.self` -- which is the
whole of the `171 -> 176` in the `gcu` column, the `1611 -> 1606` in `none` and the
`426 -> 431` accelerated. It is the one change here selected by a census of the
pipeline under test rather than by a probe standing in for it. Both halves of the
paired
Qwen-Image-2512 flagos cohort on the S60 (`torch_fl` + `diffusers`,
`FLAGOS_LOG=dispatch,fallback`) log `cpu_fallback` before their first prompt, and
the two logs agree operator for operator: **62 `cpu_fallback` calls in exactly four
operators -- `aten::where` 56, `aten::nonzero` 2, `aten::index` 2 and `aten::all`
2** -- against 489,770 dispatch records in the first half and 429,692 in the
second. No fifth operator appears in either log. Within this conf
`gcu_register.inc` moves 178 -> 183 `m.impl` lines, and `gcu_flaggems_register.inc`
keeps its 248 while its banner moves 97 -> 100: three of the five (`all`,
`nonzero`, `where.self`) were on the list of FlagGems ops `gcu_register.inc`
already claims, so claiming them natively is what takes them off it. The
reconciliations above are what the tree now reads: `255 = 248 + 7` and
`176 = 183 - 7`. The siblings stay where they were: `where.self_out`, `all.dim`
and `all.dims` are already on `flaggems`, and `all.out`, `all.all_out`,
`nonzero.out` and `nonzero_static.out` stay on `none` because the pipeline does not
call them. This change neither adds nor removes a FlagGems route, but neither was
the survey re-run against the cohort the four earlier changes left: its kept set is
the 257 routes that predate the two the third change moves off `flaggems`, so the
per-operator results below describe a cohort two operators wider than the one the
conf ships.

### Backend priority

1. `flaggems` -- FlagGems Triton kernel through the Python bridge
2. `gcu` -- native topsaten kernel
3. `none` -- not registered on PrivateUse1; ATen `cpu_fallback`

### Runtime overrides

```bash
FLAGOS_LOG=dispatch                 # print "[flagos dispatch] <op> -> <backend>"
FLAGOS_OP_abs=flaggems                # force one op onto a backend (dots -> __)
FLAGOS_BACKEND_CONFIG=/path/to.conf   # force a different conf (testing only)
```

### Native kernels for the six measured CPU fallbacks

The eleven `none` -> `gcu` moves recorded above came from a census of the host
round trips a real model makes, not from the survey. `FLAGOS_LOG=fallback`
over a 50-step Qwen-Image-2512 run at 1024x1024 lists six operators and no
seventh, which is the set `scripts/codegen/codegen_gcu.py` was taught to serve:
`arange` (three overloads, from `at::native::compute_arange_size` on the host
plus `topsatenArange`), the in-place writes `zero_` -> `topsatenZero`,
`fill_.Scalar` / `fill_.Tensor` -> `topsatenFill_` and `masked_fill_.Scalar` /
`masked_fill_.Tensor` -> `topsatenMasked_fill`, `linalg_vector_norm` ->
`topsatenLinalgVectorNorm`, and the two complex views. The in-place writes are
what `torch.zeros` / `ones` / `full` decompose into on a device, so they are
worth more than their own call count; the complex views matter because a view op
on the `cpu_fallback` path is *copied*, so its result stops aliasing its input.
`view_as_real` and `view_as_complex` are the two handwritten registrations in
`csrc/aten/strided_ops.cc`: every category template the generator emits ends in
a `topsaten::` call, so a pure metadata alias is not expressible in it, and the
generator lists both in `METADATA_OPS`. The `TopsatenArangeDtype` predicate
accepts Float / Int / Short / Char / Byte / Half / BFloat16 only, so int64 and
float64 `arange` stay on the host path. The full measurement, including the
1-ULP bound on a fractional `arange` step and the probe coverage, is in
`docs/reference/operator-support.md`; the `NATIVE_TRITON_GAPS["gcu"]` entries
for `arange`, `zero_` and the two `fill_` overloads stay, because a gap entry
only takes an op off FlagGems and for the factory family it is what *selects*
the vendor.

### Native kernels for the in-place arithmetic operators

The last three `none` -> `gcu` moves came from a second census, this one over a
*training* step rather than an inference pipeline. Two Adam steps over a
five-parameter model, run once with `foreach=True` and once with `foreach=False`,
logged 45 `cpu_fallback` calls before the change and 11 after, with the 25
`aten::add` and 10 `aten::mul` entries gone and matching 25 `add.out -> gcu` and
10 `mul.out -> gcu` dispatch lines in their place; both losses are byte-identical
across the two runs (`-32.7952`, `-51.3676`), so the reroute changed the route
and not the numbers. The remaining 11 are `index_select` (4),
`embedding_dense_backward` (4), `index_fill_` (2) and `nonzero_static` (1), none
of which the optimizer itself produces.

The ops are worth more than three routes suggest, because one kernel serves both
the explicit `out=` spelling and the in-place one: ATen gives `add_.Tensor`,
`sub_.Tensor` and `mul_.Tensor` no PrivateUse1 registration of their own, and
their composite redispatches onto `add.out` / `sub.out` / `mul.out` with
`out=self`. The conf's `add_.Tensor`, `add_.Scalar` and `mul_.*` / `sub_.*` lines
predate this and are inert -- the dispatcher never sees those spellings -- which
is why the fallbacks looked invisible in a log that prints the schema name rather
than the overload. On a 4096x4096 in-place `add_` the device path measures
**0.507 ms/call** against **114.185 ms/call** for an int64 operand, which takes
the host path by construction and is the in-run control: **225.3x**. The full
measurement -- the nine in-place spellings, both broadcasts, five dtypes, a
strided-view write, the explicit `out=` forms including a zero-size and a
differently-shaped `out`, the narrowing rejections, and the `resize_` and
`copy_` defects this path reaches -- is in `docs/reference/operator-support.md`.
Nothing here is GCU-specific in the shared code: the `resize_` and `copy_` fixes
land on Ascend, MUSA, DCU, MetaX, PPU and Tsingmicro too, and those platforms are
**not revalidated**.

## Measurement Method

`tests/manual/flaggems_overload_survey.py` (harness v4) was run against the GCU
conf as it stood *before* the measured gap set was applied: 374 `flaggems`
routes, seven profiles per overload, 2,618 cases total.

That draft is a transient working-tree version of
`torch_fl/configs/backends_gcu.conf` and is not byte-recoverable now. The survey
records both the path and the hash it read --
`"conf": ".../torch_fl/configs/backends_gcu.conf"`,
`"conf_sha256": "82f801778c392eafa6aba7f581cdbcaa4f633ae5766b7796efc2c9cd25bfb8d8"`
-- and `82f801778c` matches neither the base commit's conf (`039fb323…`) nor the
one this change ships (`7b87541e…`, later `74aab449…`). It was overwritten when
the final conf was
regenerated. What survives is the per-op JSON, which stays the auditable
evidence.

Its route count is the un-gapped candidate set, and it reconciles with the
shipped conf: **374 - 117 - 2 = 255**, where 117 = 81 ops wrong on a
`float16`/`float32` profile plus 36 ops wrong only for `int64` with a topsaten
kernel to fall back to -- precisely the ops the measurement sent back to the
vendor, as broken out below -- and the further 2 are the Group C gaps added
after the survey (see "Group C" below).
Those two are invisible to this harness by construction: every one of its seven
profiles is at most 32 rows wide, and the defect is a launch-grid axis limit
that only a real workload reaches. The 76 `int64`-only failures left on FlagGems
and the 60 unexercised routes were candidates at measurement time and are
candidates in the shipped conf; they were never part of that 117.

| Profile | dtype | shape | layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2d-f32` | float32 | 32x32 | contiguous |
| `4d-f32` | float32 | 2x3x16x16 | contiguous |
| `1d-f32` | float32 | 32 | contiguous |
| `2d-f16` | float16 | 32x32 | contiguous |
| `2d-i64` | int64 | 32x32 | contiguous |
| `2d-bool` | bool | 32x32 | contiguous |
| `2d-f32-strided` | float32 | 32x32 | strided |

Survey summary: **374 registered, 314 tested, 239 basic-executable, 121 strict**.

| Verdict | Ops | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `STRICT` | 121 | every valid profile matches the CPU reference within tolerance |
| `BASIC_ONLY` | 118 | runs, but at least one valid profile is outside tolerance |
| `FAILED` | 75 | no valid profile produced a correct result |
| `UNTESTED` | 60 | the harness could not construct a valid case for any profile |

Verdicts decide *whether* a route works; they do not decide *whether to gap it*,
because a route that is wrong only for int64 still carries a working float32
path. The routing decision therefore used a second, profile-aware pass:

| Class | Ops | Route taken |
|---|---:|---|
| clean on every exercised profile | 121 | stays on `flaggems` |
| wrong on a float16/float32 profile | 81 | reverted to the vendor route |
| wrong only for int64/bool, native topsaten kernel exists | 36 | reverted to `gcu` |
| wrong only for int64/bool, no topsaten kernel | 76 | stays on `flaggems` (see below) |

The 60 `UNTESTED` ops are disjoint from all four rows: none of them produced a
valid case on any profile, so they are counted nowhere above. They are all
shape/metadata ops (`avg_pool2d(_backward)`, `col2im`, `reflection_pad*`,
`native_group_norm*`, `scatter.reduce`, `_thnn_fused_lstm_cell`,
`_scaled_dot_product_*_backward`, ...). They are **not** covered by this
measurement and are not individually gapped; they stay on FlagGems and are
listed under "Not covered" below.

121 + 81 + 112 + 60 = 374, and 81 + 36 = 117 of the 227 gap entries come from
this measurement; 2 more come from the Group C scale failures measured on
Qwen-Image-2512 (below), and the remaining 108 are the pre-existing entries.

### Group C -- correct at every dtype, broken at scale

The seven-profile survey above cannot see this family: its widest profile is 32
rows, and the defect is in the launch grid the enflame backend builds from a
data dimension. GCU's grid limits are far below CUDA's -- `grid.x` 65535
against `2**31-1`, `grid.y` 255 against 65535 -- so a kernel launched once per
row (or per 8-row tile) passes the survey and raises on a real workload.

Measured on the S60 with `torch._softmax(x, -1, False)` on bf16:

| Input | Leading dim product `M` | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| `(1, 24, 2729, 2729)` | 65496 | PASS |
| `(1, 24, 2731, 2731)` | 65544 | FAIL `grid.x Required 65544` |
| `(1, 24, 4114, 4114)` | 98736 | FAIL `grid.x Required 98736` |

The non-inner kernel has the same defect on the other axis: a softmax that is
not over the last dimension launches with `grid = (M, cdiv(K, TILE_K), 1)`, so
`(24, 4114, 4114)` over dim 0 fails with `grid.y Required 2067`.

| Op | Kernel and launch | Failure | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_softmax` | `softmax_kernel_inner`, `grid = (M, 1, 1)` | `grid.x` above 65535 | `flaggems` -> `gcu` |
| `linalg_vector_norm` | `l2_norm_kernel`, `grid = (cdiv(M, BLOCK_M),)`, `BLOCK_M <= 8` | `grid.x` above 524280 | `flaggems` -> `gcu` |

Both were reached from Qwen-Image-2512 on the S60: `_softmax` on
`(1, 24, 4114, 4114)` from `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` in every one of the
60 transformer blocks, and `linalg_vector_norm` via `F.normalize(x, dim=1)` in
diffusers' `QwenImageRMS_norm` on the VAE decode at `(1, 128, 1, 1024, 1024)`,
`M = 1048576`, failing with `grid.x Required 131072`.

`topsatenSoftmaxForward` serves every shape above -- it has no grid to size --
so `_softmax` goes back to the vendor kernel. That was originally the only
native destination for the pair: `linalg_vector_norm` had no topsaten kernel at
the time, so its gap landed on `none` and the call reached `cpu_fallback`, and
the vendor API itself was not the missing piece -- topsaten carries
`topsteL2Norm`, but `topste` is not wired into the generator. It is now served
by `topsatenLinalgVectorNorm` instead (see "Native kernels for the six measured
CPU fallbacks" under Routing Configuration), so this gap no longer costs a host
round trip.

## Test Results

### Routing

```bash
FLAGOS_LOG=dispatch python -c "
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F, torch_fl
x = torch.randn(32, 32, device='flagos:0')
y = F.silu(x); y = torch.abs(x); y = torch.relu_(x)
print(torch.sum(x, dim=1).sum().item())
"
```

```
[flagos] loading backend config from .../torch_fl/configs/backends_gcu.conf
[flagos dispatch] randn -> gcu
[flagos dispatch] silu -> flagos_python
[flagos dispatch] abs -> gcu
[flagos dispatch] relu_ -> flagos_python
[flagos dispatch] sum.dim_IntList -> gcu
[flagos dispatch] sum -> gcu
```

`silu` and `relu_` take FlagGems; `abs` and `sum.dim_IntList` take the native
kernel because the gap set reverted them. On the base commit's conf both were
`gcu  # gcu`, so `silu -> flagos_python` is the reroute this change is about and
`abs -> gcu` is the one the measurement sent back. `randn` is native in both
configs and is printed only as the buffer the probe starts from.
`[flagos] loading backend config from ...` is printed once per process and names
the conf that decided the routes.

The two `sum` lines are the same call: this PyTorch build reaches
`sum.dim_IntList` first and its native kernel then dispatches the inner
`sum`.

## Failure Families

Every entry added to `NATIVE_TRITON_GAPS["gcu"]` came from one of the families
below. Reproduce any of them by forcing the op back onto FlagGems:

```bash
FLAGOS_OP_asin=flaggems FLAGOS_LOG=dispatch python -c "
import torch, torch_fl
torch.asin(torch.randn(32, 32, device='flagos:0'))
"
```

### 1. GCU300 front end rejects a 64-bit type in the kernel IR (largest family)

The compiler emits `error: 64-bit data type not supported on GCU300!` and the
runtime surfaces it to Python as `RuntimeError: Pipeline run failed: PassManager
execution failed`. The rejected type is a pointer parameter, so the *operand
dtype* is what has to be avoided; the op itself is fine for f16/f32/i32/bool.
Reproduced by every reduction, scan and index overload whose kernel carries an
index accumulator: `nonzero`, `argmax`, `argmin`, `count_nonzero`, `_unique2`,
`unique_dim`, `unique_consecutive`, `topk`, `median`, `nanmedian`, `max.dim`,
`min.dim`, `mode`, `kthvalue`, `range`, `repeat_interleave.Tensor`,
`unfold_backward`, `index_copy(_)`, `sum.out`, `var.correction`,
`var_mean.correction`, `_weight_norm_interface(_backward)`, `norm.Scalar`,
`norm.ScalarOpt_dim`, `native_layer_norm`, `mse_loss`, and the `scatter`/`renorm`
family. Measured on all seven profiles for `nonzero`; on the float profiles only
for the rest.

### 2. `arith.maxsi` is unimplemented in the GCU300 backend (hard compiler abort)

```
add logic to support op arith.maxsi
UNREACHABLE executed at .../third_party/enflame/triton_gcu/triton_gcu300/lib/Analysis/PtrAnalysis.cpp:1711!
```

An abort, not an exception: the process exits with SIGABRT, so the op cannot be
caught at the Python level. Reproduced on **every** profile, all dtypes, by
`_adaptive_avg_pool2d`. Nine further ops are in the same family but abort in the
elementwise lowering instead (family 3).

### 3. `unsupported extern elementwise` (hard compiler abort)

```
unsupported extern elementwise: __nv_asinf
UNREACHABLE executed at .../TritonToGCU/ElementwiseFusionOpToGCU.cpp:874!
```

The enflame backend does not lower the libm externs `flag_gems` emits for the
inverse-trig and special-function families. Reproduced by `asin`, `asin_`,
`erf`-adjacent specials and the `special_chebyshev_*` /
`special_shifted_chebyshev_*` / `special_hermite_polynomial_h` group.

### 4. Driver-level process death (SIGSEGV / SIP abort)

```
EE: [tid:498312] efdrv/src/driver/dtu_context_obj.cc:693:submit_sip_assertion_task
    ##abort as Detected SIP assert###
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  Detected SIP assert!!!
```

Reproduced by `addr` on the 1d profile (SIGABRT), and by
`_batch_norm_no_update` and `native_batch_norm` (SIGSEGV, exit status -11).
The harness truncates captured stderr at 300 bytes, so for the two
batch-norm ops the recorded evidence is the exit status plus the process's last
stderr output (FlagGems' `active Triton backend does not provide a replay
benchmarker` warning); the faulting frame is **not** in the record. They are
gapped because they kill the process, but the signal is the whole of the
evidence.

### 5. Measured wrong answers on float profiles

These run to completion and return the wrong tensor, which is the reason they
must not be inferred from a "did it raise" test:

| Op | Measured difference from CPU |
|---|---|
| `elu`, `elu_`, `elu_backward` | `max_diff` 0.38 -- 0.89 on f32, 0.70 on f16 |
| `histc` | `max_diff` 32 -- 1536 (bin counts) |
| `_softmax_backward_data`, `_log_softmax_backward_data` | returns `torch.int8` where `torch.float32` is expected |
| `sum.out` | returns shape `(32, 32)` where the scalar output shape `()` is expected |
| `_pdist_backward`, `_weight_norm_interface(_backward)` | outside tolerance on all float profiles |
| `addmm.out`, `addmm_`, `silu_backward` | outside tolerance on all float profiles |
| `tril.out`, `tril_`, `triu`, `triu_` | outside tolerance on all float profiles |

### 6. `flag_gems` wrapper refuses an input ATen accepts

Not device defects -- the FlagGems Python wrapper is stricter than the ATen
schema, so a caller that works on CPU raises on GCU:

- `topk`: `AssertionError: Currently only support topk in last dimension`
- `special_modified_bessel_k0(.out)`: `AssertionError: Tensors must be CUDA tensors`
- `dequantize.self`: `NotImplementedError: Could not run 'aten::int_repr' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend`
- `_linalg_eigvals`: `RuntimeError: PyTorch was compiled without CUDA support`

### 7. Scan family (pre-existing gap entries)

`cumsum`, `cumsum.out`, `cumprod`, `cumprod_`, `cummax`, `cummin`,
`logcumsumexp`, `logcumsumexp.out` were already in the gap set before this
measurement and remain there.

## int64-only failures left on FlagGems

76 overloads are correct for float16, float32, int32 and bool and fail **only**
for an int64 operand, and have no topsaten kernel to fall back to. Gapping them
would send their float path to `cpu_fallback` as well, so they stay on FlagGems.
The consequence is explicit: these ops **raise** `Pipeline run failed:
PassManager execution failed` for an int64 operand, where the previous
configuration served the same call through `cpu_fallback`. The set is dominated
by ops a float model never hands an int64 tensor:

```
abs_ acosh addcmul addcmul_ angle asinh atan2 atanh ceil.out ceil_
clamp_max clamp_min digamma exp2 floor.out floor_ floor_divide.Scalar fmax
fmax.out fmin fmin.out gcd_ gt_.Scalar gt_.Tensor isin.Scalar_Tensor isinf
isnan isneginf lcm lcm_ logical_and_ logical_not logical_not_ logical_or
logical_xor logical_xor_ logit logsumexp lt_.Scalar lt_.Tensor masked_scatter
masked_scatter_ max min nan_to_num neg_ new_ones pow.Scalar pow_.Tensor prod
prod.dim_int rad2deg relu_ remainder.Scalar_Tensor rsub.Scalar sgn_ signbit
sinc slice_backward special_airy_ai special_chebyshev_polynomial_u.n_scalar
special_i0e special_i1 special_modified_bessel_k1
special_shifted_chebyshev_polynomial_v special_xlog1py sum.IntList_out tan
threshold threshold_ threshold_backward trace trunc_ xlogy.Scalar_Other
xlogy.Scalar_Self xlogy.Tensor
```

The 36 overloads in the same class that *do* have a topsaten kernel are gapped
and route to `gcu`, where the generated kernel's `TopsatenSupportsDtype` guard
round-trips int64 through the CPU. That is slower than FlagGems but correct, and
it keeps int64 working for the three highest-traffic names in the group
(`abs`, `neg`, `sum.dim_IntList`), which the previous configuration also served:

```
abs acos addmm amax amin atan ceil cos cosh erf exp expm1 flip floor
fmod.Scalar log log10 log1p log2 logical_and logical_or mse_loss_backward neg
pow.Tensor_Scalar pow.Tensor_Tensor reciprocal relu remainder.Scalar sigmoid sin
sinh sqrt sum.dim_IntList tanh tril trunc
```

## Known Issues

### FlagGems cannot compile any kernel that is handed an int64 tensor

**Root cause**: the GCU300 front end in `triton_gcu300` rejects 64-bit types in
kernel IR. It is a property of the compiler, not of `flag_gems`: the same
`flag_gems` kernel compiles on CPU/CUDA Triton backends, and the equivalent
hand-written Triton kernel fails identically on this device.

Reproduced locally:

```bash
FLAGOS_OP_abs=flaggems python -c "
import torch, torch_fl
torch.abs(torch.tensor([-1, -2, 3], device='flagos:0'))
"
```

```
RuntimeError: Pipeline run failed: PassManager execution failed
```

**Impact**: any FlagGems route whose op is handed an int64 tensor raises. Where
topsaten has a kernel the op is gapped and the call succeeds on the vendor path;
where it does not, the op raises rather than falling back (76 overloads, listed
above).

**Resolution**: not fixable in this repository. Routing is per operator and the
rejected type is the operand dtype, so there is no per-dtype fallback to hang
this on without a dispatcher change. The gap set is the mitigation; the
remainder is documented rather than hidden.

### FlagGems `elu` returns wrong values on the enflame backend

**Root cause**: the lowered `elu` kernel produces values that disagree with the
CPU reference on all four float profiles. Whether this is the flagtree lowering
or the `flag_gems` formulation was not isolated; the observable is what the
routing decision was made on.

Reproduced by the survey's `2d-f32` profile, dtype float32:

```
max_diff=0.8942340614211499        # 2d-f32, torch.elu
max_diff=0.7372526526451111        # 2d-f32, torch.elu
```

**Impact**: silent wrong answers on every float profile, including `elu_backward`.
**Resolution**: `elu`, `elu_`, `elu_backward` moved to
`NATIVE_TRITON_GAPS["gcu"]`. A wrong answer is worse than a slow one, so this
family was treated as more urgent than the crashes.

### 60 FlagGems routes could not be exercised by the harness

**Impact**: the measurement above does not cover these ops -- shapes and
metadata-driven overloads the generic harness cannot construct a valid call for:
`_conv_depthwise2d`, `_efficient_attention_backward`,
`_embedding_bag_dense_backward`, `_flash_attention_backward`, `_masked_scale`,
`_scaled_dot_product_{cudnn,efficient,flash}_attention_backward`,
`_sparse_semi_structured_mm`, `_thnn_fused_lstm_cell(_backward_impl)`,
`_upsample_bicubic2d_aa_backward`, `addmm.dtype(_out)`, `addmv`,
`avg_pool2d/3d(_backward)`, `bincount`, `clamp`, `col2im`, `cudnn_convolution`,
`mv`, `native_batch_norm_backward`, `native_group_norm(_backward)`,
`nll_loss2d_*`, `reflection_pad1d/2d/3d(_backward)`, `replication_pad1d/3d`,
`rot90`, `scatter.reduce`, `scatter_reduce.two(_out)`, `scatter_reduce_.two`,
`upsample_linear1d_backward`, `fractional_max_pool2d(_backward)`,
`max_pool2d/3d_with_indices`, `max_unpool2d`, `diagonal_backward`,
`glu_backward`, `index_reduce_`, `affine_grid_generator`,
`rrelu_with_noise_backward`, `softplus_backward`, `lift`, `polar`, and the
`special_scaled_modified_bessel_k1` pair.

**Resolution**: not gapped. They stay on FlagGems, and this document records that
they are **not measured** rather than claiming they pass. A targeted harness is
the follow-up.

### `active Triton backend does not provide a replay benchmarker`

```
RuntimeWarning: active Triton backend does not provide a replay benchmarker; falling back to event timing
```

The enflame Triton backend does not implement the replay benchmarking API
FlagGems' `libentry` prefers. Timing falls back to event measurement. Correctness
is unaffected and no route was changed for it.

## Not covered

- **Other GCU hosts**: the S60 is the only Enflame machine available to this
  change. No GCU400 or multi-card claim is made, and the device-1 (`flagos:1`)
  paths were exercised only indirectly through the unified RNG suite.
- **The 60 unexercised routes** above.
- **torch.compile on FlagGems-routed ops**: `test_compile.py` passes, but its
  cases are not selected by the FlagGems route set, so it does not establish
  that a FlagGems-routed op survives `torch.compile`.
- **Non-GCU platforms**: no route was measured for Ascend, MUSA, DCU, MetaX or
  PPU, and no route was changed for them.

## Full CI manifest reproduction (local)

Every group of `.github/configs/gcu.yml` was run locally on the S60 against the
final tree, in one uninterrupted pass, in manifest order. All eight exit 0.

| # | Group | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check isolated GCU environment | `bash .github/scripts/set_env_gcu.sh` | see below |
| 2 | Vendor backend, main ops | `pytest tests/integration/ops/ -m "(anyplatform or main_ops) and not flaggems_python and not flaggems_cpp"` | 595 passed, 32 skipped, 499 deselected, 2 xfailed, 2 xpassed |
| 3 | FlagGems runtime path, main ops | `FLAGOS_USE_FLAGGEMS=1 pytest tests/integration/ops/ -m "flaggems and main_ops"` | 9 passed, 4 skipped, 1116 deselected, 1 xpassed |
| 4 | Unified RNG | `pytest tests/integration/ops/test_rng_dispatch.py -m main_ops` | 111 passed, 4 skipped, 1 deselected, 1 xpassed |
| 5 | General (factory ops) | `pytest tests/integration/test_factory_ops.py` | 46 passed |
| 6 | Unified AMP contract | `pytest tests/integration/test_amp_contract.py -m amp` | 27 passed |
| 7 | Unified math-bits contract | `pytest tests/integration/test_math_bits_contract.py -m math_bits` | 12 passed |
| 8 | torch.compile | `pytest tests/integration/test_compile.py` | 29 passed, 18 skipped |

Two of these groups failed on the first attempt, for reasons that are not defects
in the shipped routes and that a reader should be able to check against this
record:

- **Group 3, 3 of 14.** `test_abs_dispatch.py`, `test_neg_dispatch.py` and
  `test_sum_dispatch.py` asserted `-> flagos_python` unconditionally, but this
  change moves `abs`, `neg` and `sum.dim_IntList` to the vendor route. They were
  rewritten to assert the route the platform configuration actually lists
  (`routed_backend(...)`), the pattern `test_add_dispatch.py` already used for
  the MUSA `add.Tensor` case. This is the positive control for the rerouting: the
  tests fail if the gap set is reverted, and the group passes after the rewrite.
- **Group 8, 1 of 29.** `test_torch_backends_entry_point_is_registered` failed
  with `AssertionError: torch_fl must register a torch.backends entry point;
  found {}` against a local `torch_fl.egg-info` baked without `entry_points.txt`.
  `setup.py egg_info` regenerated it and the group passes. A stale local build
  artifact, not a property of the change.

### Unit tests

`pytest tests/unit/` is not part of the GCU CI manifest, which runs integration
groups only. Run on the same tree it is **2 failed, 317 passed, 97 skipped**, and
both failures pre-date this change:

- `test_gen_vendor_confs.py::test_shipped_confs_are_up_to_date` reports
  `stale: ['backends_ascend.conf']`. Run on a pristine `flagos/main` worktree
  (`bc39a83`), the same test reports
  `stale: ['backends_gcu.conf', 'backends_ascend.conf']`, so both halves are
  pre-existing and this change repairs the GCU one. The repair is not just the
  regeneration: that worktree's generator wants to emit 88 GCU `flaggems` routes
  and not one of them had a registration behind it, so regenerating there would
  have produced a conf whose `flaggems` routes dispatch to an empty slot. The
  change supplies the missing `gcu_flaggems_register.inc` and the measured gap
  set first, and only then regenerates. Ascend is left alone: it is a different
  platform and out of scope.
- `test_profiler_privateuse1.py::test_guard_stream_is_real_not_synthetic` fails
  with `assert 0 != 0` (`csrc/runtime/guard.h` returns stream id 0); unrelated to
  routing and untouched here.

`.github/scripts/set_env_gcu.sh` was run end to end against a scratch venv
(`TORCH_FL_VENV_ROOT` pointing at an empty directory, `CI_STAGE=integration`), so
the whole provisioning path ran for real rather than being read. Every step
before the final import check succeeded:

| Step | Observed |
|---|---|
| TopsRider SDK discovery | `TOPS_HOME=/opt/tops`, `lib/libtopsrt.so` + `include/gcu/topsaten/topsaten.h` found |
| topsaten library | `/usr/lib/libtopsaten.so` |
| Device node | `/dev/gcu0` present |
| venv bootstrap | `provision-venv/bin/python`, Python 3.12 |

| `torch_gcu` excluded | `find_spec("torch_gcu") is None` asserted clean |
| NVIDIA triton removed | `pip show triton` empty before the flagtree install |
| flagtree | `flagtree-0.6.1+enflame3.6` installed from the FlagOS index |
| FlagGems | `flag_gems-5.4.0rc2.post1+g3c6f7537d` built from git and installed |
| FlagGems deps | `packaging`, `PyYAML==6.0.1`, `sqlalchemy==2.0.48` |
| Triton import check | `Triton: 3.6.0 (backends: ['enflame'])`, `flag_gems: installed` |

The last row is the one step the box could not reach unassisted: the check
aborted with the glibc 2.38 error described under
[Host toolchain caveat](#host-toolchain-caveat-measurement-box-only). After
applying that same local-only retarget to the scratch venv's `libtriton.so`, the
script's own verification snippet — the exact heredoc it runs, asserting
`"enflame" in triton.backends.backends` and that `flag_gems` is importable —
passes verbatim, which is the output quoted above. Everything else in the run is
unmodified, and the failure is a property of the 22.04 host, not of the script.

The remaining statement to be exact about: this is a *local* reproduction of the
provisioning path, not a CI run. `.github/configs/gcu.yml` has not executed this
change yet.

### Generator idempotency

Both generators were run twice in a row and the second run produced no change:

- `scripts/codegen/gen_vendor_confs.py` -- `backends_gcu.conf` sha256 identical across
  the two runs (`74aab449...`), and `--check` exits 0.
- `scripts/codegen/codegen_gcu_flaggems.py` -- `gcu_flaggems_register.inc` sha256
  identical across the two runs (`9c9c99d0...`), and `--check` exits 0.
- `scripts/codegen/codegen_gcu.py` has no `--check` mode, so its idempotency was
  proven by re-running it three times and comparing the three generated files:
  byte-identical each time (`74aab449...` conf, `35c8a37e...` kernels,
  `f961aff0...` register).

## Summary

- `backends_gcu.conf` went from 152 to **431 accelerated routes** out of 2037
  (7.5% -> 21.2%): 255 `flaggems`, 176 `gcu`, 1606 `none`.
- 374 FlagGems routes were measured across seven profiles each: 121 are clean on
  every exercised profile, 81 are wrong at float16/float32 and were reverted to
  the vendor route, and 112 are wrong only for int64/bool (36 of them reverted
  because topsaten has a kernel, 76 kept on FlagGems because it does not).
- A census of a real workload replaced the survey for the last nineteen moves:
  a 50-step Qwen-Image-2512 run at 1024x1024 made **80,536 `cpu_fallback` calls
  in exactly six operators**, two Adam steps over a five-parameter model made
  **45, of which 35 were the in-place arithmetic the optimizer runs every step**,
  and the pipeline's own warm-up on the S60 made **62 in four operators**.
  The six reach a kernel on the device; of the 35, 25 `aten::add` and 10
  `aten::mul` now do too, and the 11 the optimizer does not produce are what
  remains.
- FlagGems is not patched or forked. Every route that could not work on the
  enflame stack was moved into `NATIVE_TRITON_GAPS["gcu"]` in the generator.
- All eight `.github/configs/gcu.yml` groups pass locally on the same tree.
